description: Which platform a product runs on, for the host search (cveFeed.tech_search): a host that shows one of a platform's products runs that platform, whatever version, so tech:php finds a WordPress host and tech:java a Tomcat host. 'names' are what a search for the platform may be typed as (tech:php, tech:dotnet); 'runtime' is the language runtime reading of cveFeed.version_sources that states the platform's own version ('java_runtime' for cveFeed.java_runtime's readings); 'products' are the products that imply it, each with 'why': the product's own documentation that says it is written in, or needs, the platform. A product is matched as a whole word of a technology name, an open port's product, a version source reading or a live route's Server, X-Powered-By or fingerprint; 'pattern' replaces the names when a bare name is ambiguous. Java's products are not listed here: they are java_runtime.JAVA_PRODUCT_RE, the same rule that makes a host a candidate for a Java runtime CVE ('products_from'). A product shown never says which version of the platform it runs: @unknown means no reading of the platform itself.

platforms.label: Java
platforms.why: Each product of JAVA_PRODUCT_RE (Tomcat, Jetty, Jenkins, the Atlassian products, Spring, WebLogic, WildFly, Elasticsearch, Kafka ...) runs on a JVM; the list and its reasons are docs/PIPELINE.md#java-runtime

products.why: WordPress is written in PHP: https://wordpress.org/about/requirements/ names the PHP release it needs
Drupal is written in PHP: https://www.drupal.org/docs/getting-started/system-requirements/php-requirements
Joomla is written in PHP: https://manual.joomla.org/docs/next/get-started/technical-requirements/
Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce are PHP applications: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/installation-guide/system-requirements
Laravel is a PHP framework: https://laravel.com/docs/deployment#server-requirements
phpMyAdmin is written in PHP: https://docs.phpmyadmin.net/en/latest/require.html
MediaWiki is written in PHP: https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Manual:Installation_requirements
Nextcloud Server is a PHP application: https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/latest/admin_manual/installation/system_requirements.html

platforms.label: .NET
platforms.note: IIS alone is not counted: it also serves static files, PHP and classic ASP. IIS with ASP.NET counts through ASP.NET's own signal (X-Powered-By: ASP.NET, X-AspNet-Version, the ASP.NET session cookie, nuclei's aspgeneric), which names the platform itself.

products.why: SharePoint Server is an ASP.NET application on IIS: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/install/hardware-and-software-requirements-2019
Exchange Server's web services (OWA, ECP, EWS) are ASP.NET applications and it requires the .NET Framework: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/plan-and-deploy/prerequisites
Umbraco is an ASP.NET CMS: https://docs.umbraco.com/umbraco-cms/fundamentals/setup/requirements
DNN (DotNetNuke) is an ASP.NET CMS: https://docs.dnncommunity.org/content/getting-started/setup/installation/requirements/index.html
Express is a Node.js web framework: https://expressjs.com/en/starter/installing.html. A bare 'Express' is matched only as the whole name, never inside another (SQL Server Express, UniFi Express)
Next.js is a React framework that runs on Node.js: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation (system requirements)
Nuxt runs on Node.js: https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/installation#prerequisites
Ghost is a Node.js CMS: https://ghost.org/docs/faq/node-versions/. Only the whole name: 'ghost' is a common word
Strapi is a Node.js headless CMS: https://docs.strapi.io/cms/installation/cli (prerequisites)
Django is a Python web framework: https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/stable/faq/install/
Flask and the Werkzeug server it ships with are Python: https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/installation/
Plone runs on Python (Zope): https://6.docs.plone.org/install/create-project-cookieplone.html (prerequisites)
Odoo is written in Python: https://www.odoo.com/documentation/master/administration/on_premise/source.html
Gunicorn is a Python WSGI server: https://docs.gunicorn.org/en/stable/install.html
Rails is a Ruby framework: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/install_ruby_on_rails.html
GitLab is a Rails application: https://docs.gitlab.com/install/requirements/ (it bundles its Ruby)
Discourse is a Rails application: https://github.com/discourse/discourse/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPER-ADVANCED.md
Redmine is a Rails application: https://www.redmine.org/projects/redmine/wiki/RedmineInstall#Requirements
